summa:
The Summa entry is not a single living thinker but the project's companion tradition: a structured, day-by-day walk through Thomas Aquinas's *Summa Theologiae*, maintained as its own vault and surfaced in the system's Curriculum tools. It is the tradition the other programs keep pointing back toward — Stump's analytic Thomism, MacIntyre's exemplary living tradition, Rohr's complementary Catholic register all presuppose a working acquaintance with Aquinas's actual arguments, and the Summa vault is where that acquaintance is built rather than assumed.

The contemporary entry point for this material is **Austin Habash**, the lecturer whose commentary anchors the year-long reading. His transcripts — a complete set covering the project's planned sequence — are the primary source the Summa pipeline ingests, segments, and indexes day by day; the lecturer's task is to guide a non-specialist reader up into competence in Aquinas's framework at a sustainable pace, which is exactly the "curriculum for climbing into maturity in a tradition" that MacIntyre's account requires and that the project treats as a precondition for any genuine inter-tradition encounter. In that sense Habash plays, for the Aquinas tradition, the role the individual thinker-agents play for theirs: the voice through which the tradition is made learnable.

Structurally, Aquinas supplies the spine that several scientific programs are being read against. Thomistic hylomorphism (form and matter co-constituting substance) and final causality (substances directed toward ends not yet realized) are the metaphysical commitments the project uses to interpret Levin's morphogenetic teleology and to give Friston's prediction-error minimization a teleological reading rather than a merely mechanical one. Aquinas's account of *beatitudo* — union as the highest human good — is the thread Stump draws to Fredrickson's positivity resonance, and his treatment of wisdom as an integrative science is the classical precedent for the project's own ambition to integrate the disciplines rather than merely federate them.

Open threads on this tradition are as much about pipeline as about doctrine: keeping the daily reading in sync with the rest of the wiki, deciding how much of the lecture commentary is publishable versus held for copyright, and working out how the Summa's question-objection-respondeo structure (a medieval engine for staging and answering rival positions) might itself be a template for the project's cross-tradition dialogues. The Summa is, after all, the original "accelerator-detector" for traditions in conflict — Aquinas systematically inhabits the strongest form of each opposing view before answering it, which is precisely the discipline the C2A2 system is trying to reproduce at machine speed.
__tradition_concept__:
In C2A2, a tradition is a community enduring across a period of time sufficient to support articulation of common goals whose achievement constitutes a practice. None of these terms is especially precise, nor should it be: “tradition” is itself a good example of a synergistic coil — a dynamic, useful tool that, for a time and for certain purposes, can be used in a way its users accept to solve problems. Different traditions may use the term differently, so long as they recognize, without contestation, its usefulness in other ways and for other purposes.

In a conscious-realist monist ontology, conscious agents are everything there is; and if they have a sense of identity over time — individually or collectively — the term “tradition” may sensibly be applied at every level. I am a tradition, insofar as I am constituted by a community of conscious agents around some enduring common goal; I am a member of larger traditions, ceteris paribus; and those traditions are members of larger communities, which as a collective may themselves be a tradition of interaction among traditions.

This flexibility is used throughout C2A2. A head of a research program may be called a tradition (say, Levin, or the Levin group), as may a larger cluster of interdisciplinary academic researchers, or a still larger group of people learning from and putting into practice the worldview emerging from such a group’s work. The fifteen-or-so thinkers gathered here as jointly pursuing something like a conscious-realist monist paradigm constitute a tradition in one sense; so does each member research group; so does each individual researcher within them.

The term’s focal meaning — perhaps now shifting in the age of AI-agent inclusion — is generally recognizably social at the human level: a group of persons who recognize one another as such.
